chat.greeting: Hi Dan — I have your March MOR data ingested (PWS CO0130035, all 31 days) and your Q4 2025 PFAS results on file. What do you need?
chat.presetQ: How much GAC bed life do we have left before changeout?
chat.presetA: Your GAC bed is currently at 8,200 bed volumes of throughput since the February 2025 changeout. Genesee's internal threshold for replacement is 12,000 BV — so you're at 68% of bed life with roughly 3,800 BV remaining. At current finished-water production (~0.42 MGD avg), that's about 5–6 months of treatment capacity. Q4 2025 post-GAC PFOA and PFOS were both non-detect, so the bed is performing well — but bed volume is your leading indicator, not effluent PFAS. Recommend requesting a Calgon vendor quote in Q2 to lock in a Q3 2026 changeout slot.
chat.presetCite: 📊 CO0130035 GAC log · Last changeout Feb 14, 2025 · Q4 2025 PFAS report

mar-data-lock.title: March 2026 MOR — Data Lock
mar-data-lock.what: What this is: Hard cutoff for entering March turbidity, UV transmittance, and disinfection readings. After this point, the dataset is finalized and submitted to the MOR report builder. Late entries require a written addendum.
mar-data-lock.footer: Source: CDPHE Reg 11 · Section 11.10 monthly reporting

compliance-pull.title: Weekly Compliance Pull
compliance-pull.what: What this is: Upstream's weekly automated ingestion of CDPHE-formatted MOR data sheets, lab returns, GAC effluent logs, and SCADA exports. Refreshes your compliance status, flags anomalies, and pre-populates this week's tasks.

callout.title: Anomaly detected
callout.body: GAC bed at 8,200 BV — 68% of changeout threshold. Auto-task created: "Review GAC breakthrough monitoring" due Wed Apr 8.

gac-bv-check.title: GAC Bed Volume Check
gac-bv-check.what: What this is: System-generated task triggered by the weekly compliance pull. GAC media throughput is at 8,200 bed volumes (68% of Genesee's 12,000 BV changeout threshold). Recommendation: confirm post-GAC PFAS still ND, and begin scheduling Q3 2026 changeout.

gac-trend-review.title: GAC Trend Review
gac-trend-review.what: What this is: Scheduled review of GAC bed volume trajectory and PFAS effluent history. Confirms vendor changeout timing for Q3 2026 and validates that the 12,000 BV internal threshold remains conservative against EPA's 4 ppt PFOA/PFOS MCL.
details: Lock vendor quote request by Apr 30

bod5-tss-pickup.title: BOD₅ + TSS — Bear Creek Effluent
bod5-tss-pickup.what: What this is: Routine weekly wastewater compliance sampling. Both samples go into the same orange-cap (no preservative) bottles. BOD₅ is your critical hold — must reach the lab within 48 hours, so we recommend a morning pickup.

callout.title: Critical hold — 48 hours
callout.body: BOD₅ samples held longer than 48 hrs are rejected by the lab. Drop at the WWTP cooler by 9 AM for the 10 AM courier.

ttham-hAA5.title: TTHM + HAA5 — Distribution System (DBP1 + DBP2)
ttham-hAA5.what: What this is: Quarterly disinfection byproduct (DBP) sampling from Tier 1 distribution sites. TTHM (total trihalomethanes) and HAA5 (haloacetic acids) are regulated under Stage 2 DBPR. Genesee uses GAC ahead of chlorination, which keeps DBPs comfortably under MCLs (80 ppb TTHM, 60 ppb HAA5).

bottle.label: None
bottle.name: 40 mL VOA vial (TTHM) + 250 mL HDPE (HAA5)
bottle.meta: Na₂S₂O₃ in-bottle · 4°C · Zero headspace for VOA · No preservative

details: TTHM 18 ppb · HAA5 9 ppb (well under MCL)

ammonia-apr9.title: Ammonia (NH₃-N) — Bear Creek Effluent
ammonia-apr9.what: What this is: Ammonia effluent sample. Bear Creek's downstream segment is salmonid-bearing and CDPHE has tightened ammonia limits to protect aquatic life. With Bear Creek temperatures rising into the 13–18°C salmonid window, ammonia toxicity sensitivity increases.

bottle.label: H₂SO₄
bottle.name: 500 mL polypropylene cylinder, yellow cap
bottle.meta: H₂SO₄ to pH < 2 · 4°C · Eurofins bottle code

callout.title: Bottle prep reminder
callout.body: Yellow caps come pre-acidified from the lab. Do not rinse. If a bottle arrives without preservative, mark it and request replacement before sampling.

ammonia-apr9.footer: Source: CDPS CO0022951 · Bear Creek aquatic life standards

mar-mor-due.title: March 2026 MOR — Submission Due

callout.title: GAC note
callout.body: GAC bed at 8,200 BV (68% of changeout threshold). All TT criteria met but include the GAC trajectory in the submission notes for CDPHE reviewer context.

ecoli-apr13.title: E. coli — Bear Creek Effluent
ecoli-apr13.what: What this is: First effluent E. coli sample of the recreation season. Bear Creek recreation use kicks in April 1 each year. 6-hour hold time — this is the tightest hold in the program. Same-day delivery only.

details: CDPS CO0022951 recreation-season E. coli limit

callout.title: 6-hour clock

bod5-apr14.title: BOD₅ — Bear Creek Effluent
bod5-apr14.what: What this is: Weekly BOD₅ effluent sample. Permit requires weekly grab samples during operating months. 48-hour critical hold.

op-cert-ceu.title: CDPHE Operator CEU — Quarterly Credit
op-cert-ceu.what: What this is: CDPHE drinking water and wastewater operator certifications require continuing education units (CEUs) to renew. This quarter's credit window closes mid-April. Confirm Dan's and the contract ORCs' CEU logs are current.

callout.title: Quick check
callout.body: Log into the CDPHE operator portal and confirm CEU credits posted from the spring AWWA Rocky Mountain Section conference. Trade associations usually take 3–4 weeks to report.

lead-copper.title: Lead / Copper — Tier 1 Customer Taps (30 sites)
lead-copper.what: What this is: Semi-annual lead/copper sampling at 30 Tier 1 customer taps under the Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR). 90th percentile results determine whether action-level exceedance protocols trigger. Genesee's lead service line inventory shows 312 lines mapped — no known full lead lines, but galvanized requiring replacement (GRR) sites are prioritized.

tss-apr17.title: TSS — Bear Creek Effluent
tss-apr17.what: What this is: Weekly TSS effluent grab sample. 7-day hold time gives some scheduling flexibility, but coordinate with BOD₅ pickups when possible to share couriers.

pfas-q1.type: PFAS Quarterly Sample · EPA Final Rule
pfas-q1.title: PFAS — Post-GAC + Entry Point to Distribution
pfas-q1.what: What this is: Q1 2026 PFAS compliance sampling. EPA's PFAS Final Rule (2024) set MCLs at 4 parts per trillion for PFOA and PFOS, with a Hazard Index for four others (PFNA, PFHxS, PFBS, HFPO-DA). Genesee samples both post-GAC and EPDS to verify the GAC is performing — Q4 2025 was non-detect across all six analytes.

bottle.label: PFAS
bottle.name: 250 mL polypropylene, PFAS-clean
bottle.meta: No preservative · 4°C · NO Teflon contact at any step

details: PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, PFHxS, PFBS, HFPO-DA
4 ppt PFOA · 4 ppt PFOS · Hazard Index for 4 others

callout.title: PFAS sampling protocol
callout.body: Field crew must avoid all Teflon, waterproof clothing with PFAS, sunscreen, and recent fast food packaging contact. Use the dedicated PFAS sampling kit only. Cross-contamination invalidates the sample.

pfas-q1.footer: Source: EPA PFAS Final Rule (Apr 2024) · CDPHE Reg 11 PFAS
